Schema Sense Studio is an independent software and creative studio in Emmett, Idaho. It builds the Sense family of apps, tools that help people make sense of trading, money, knowledge, and daily life. It also publishes the books, music, and games that come out of the same workshop, and makes physical things on the shop bench: 3D-designed, 3D-printed pieces today, with more hands-on crafts on the way.

The Studio

Where it is, what it is, and why

Where

The studio sits outside Emmett, in unincorporated Gem County, Idaho: high desert, farm country, and a workshop full of tools. No tower, no campus, no venture money. Just a small studio in a small town, building for anyone, anywhere.

What

A family of apps that share one name and one promise: the Sense apps. Trade Sense, Know Sense, Tally Sense, Dollars And Sense, and their brothers each take one tangled subject and give it a clear pattern you can actually use.

Under the same roof, the studio also publishes books, music, and games, and makes physical things in the shop: 3D models designed and printed in-house, with wood burning, CNC, woodwork, and metalwork planned as the bench grows. One LLC, several crafts, all of it made on purpose.

Why

Forty years in information technology, and a second education bought the hard way in the markets and in life, produced a lot of hard-earned understanding. Knowledge like that should not sit in one man's head and retire with him.

So the studio exists to hand it on: to turn what one person learned the expensive way into tools that cost the next person a lot less.

The Name

Schema. Sense. Studio.

Every word in the name is doing a job. Together they are the studio's whole method, stated in three words.

Word One · The Pattern

Schema

A schema is the underlying pattern, the blueprint underneath a thing that makes it understandable. Databases run on schemas. Minds do too: we understand new things by fitting them to a pattern we already hold. The studio's first job, on every project, is to find that pattern.

Word Two · The Promise

Sense

Sense is the family name, carried by every app: Trade Sense, Know Sense, Life Sense. It is also the promise. A subject has been handled right when it finally makes sense: when the numbers add up, the picture clears, and you know what to do next.

Word Three · The Workshop

Studio

A studio is where a maker works: part workshop, part drafting table, part recording room. It says these things are crafted deliberately, by a person with his name on the door, not mass-produced by a faceless company. Apps, books, music, and games all come off the same bench, and the shop bench turns out printed and crafted pieces of its own.

Find the pattern. Make it make sense. Build it by hand.
That is the name, and it is also the work.

Beyond the Apps

One studio, several crafts

Books

Writing is in the studio's charter, right alongside the software. Books in progress carry the same method as the apps: real experience, organized until it makes sense, then handed on.

Music

Songs and lyrics are part of the founding mix. The studio is a musician's workshop too, and its music work is published under the same name and the same standard.

Games

Tabletop games like Floor Wars, designed and playtested at the studio table with family and friends, plus the gaming tools in the app family: Battle Sense and War List Sense. Play is serious work here.

The Workshop

Not everything the studio makes lives on a screen. There is a real shop on the property, with real machines in it, and a growing list of crafts the studio is taking up. The same rule applies as everywhere else here: what is running today says so, and what is still a plan is labeled a plan.

On the bench today

Designed, printed, and finished in the studio's own shop.

3D model design

Original models designed from scratch: game pieces, parts, and useful objects, modeled digitally before a single gram of filament is spent.

3D printing

Those models come off the printer in the shop, layer by layer: prototypes, tabletop pieces, and practical prints, including pieces for the studio's own games.

Laser engraving

Designs burned in with light: marks, lettering, and artwork engraved into finished pieces on the shop's laser.

On the horizon

Crafts the studio is taking up next, one bench at a time.

Wood burning

Pyrography by hand: artwork and lettering burned into wood, a natural partner to the laser work and the wood shop.

CNC machining, one day

Computer-guided cutting and carving is on the roadmap: the machine is a someday purchase, and the plans for it are already forming.

Woodwork

Real lumber, real joinery: boards, boxes, and built things from the wood side of the shop.

Metalwork

Cutting, shaping, and welding metal: the heaviest bench in the plan, and the one that rounds out the shop.

The Founder

Built by a man who did the work

Bryon D. Scott spent 40 years in Information Technology Engineering, including years with four Fortune 500 companies: AT&T, Intel, Micron, and Boise Cascade. The work ran deep: data engineering, analytics, business intelligence, and software validation. An ideas man and a systems thinker, he learned how complicated systems behave, and how to make them understandable. He came from humble beginnings, and counts himself blessed all along the way, even through the tragedies and the pain. Schema Sense Studio is where that lifetime of seeing patterns now gets built into things other people can use.

In 2026 he turned that experience outward and founded Schema Sense Studio LLC in Emmett, Idaho. The studio is deliberately small and deliberately honest: what is released says so, what is not does not pretend, and everything carries the same promise his career taught him.

Away from the keyboard he is a maker: 3D printing, laser engraving, and music (clarinet, saxophone, piano, guitar, and more), with wood burning, CNC, woodwork, and metalwork in his sights. The shop and the software come from the same hands.

In his own framing, from the studio's earliest days: what I am and know, I offer to you.
